title: Coefficient biduality map is compatible with shifts and triangles
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, small in the chosen universe, with a sheaf of commutative rings, and write $\mathcal D=D(\mathcal O)$ for its unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the derived internal Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and put $V^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(V,\mathcal O[0])$. Let $d_V:V\to V^{\vee\vee}$ be the transpose of coefficient evaluation after interchanging the tensor factors by Koszul symmetry [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. Then the natural transformation $d:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\to(-)^{\vee\vee}$ commutes with the signed shift comparisons for derived internal Hom, and for every distinguished triangle $V\to W\to Z\to V[1]$ its three components give a morphism to the triangle obtained by applying $(-)^{\vee\vee}$, including the square on the connecting map. Slice restriction to the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O|_U)$ of an object $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] carries this morphism of triangles to the corresponding one on the slice. Moreover let $R$ be a commutative ring acting centrally on $\mathcal O$, let $s\in R$, and let $\mathcal T\subset\mathcal D$ be a full $R$-linear triangulated subcategory preserved by $(-)^\vee$, with $R$-linear shifts. The transformation and these compatibilities descend to the raw scalar localization $\mathcal T[1/s]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Thus, both in $\mathcal D$ and in $\mathcal T[1/s]$, the class of objects with invertible $d_V$ is closed under shifts and two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles. No claim that an arbitrary $d_V$ is invertible is made.

source.place: Tags 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), 0A97 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), and 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); compatibility of the evaluation-defined double-dual map with the shifted cone matrices, expanded from these constructions. Scalar-localized version serves proof paragraph 3 of blueprint lem-coef-rational-retract-evaluation.

proof.text: Fix a K-injective resolution $\mathcal O[0]\to I$ and put $T(E)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I)$ for every complex $E$. The derived-Hom definition identifies $QT(E)$ with $(QE)^\vee$ and $QT^2(E)$ with $(QE)^{\vee\vee}$: in both occurrences only the target $I$ must be K-injective. For a quasi-isomorphism $u:E\to E'$, apply the well-definedness lemma with target map $1_I$ to see that $T(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and apply it once more to $T(u)$ for $T^2(u)$. Thus $T^2$ descends to the actual functor $F=(-)^{\vee\vee}$. These are the canonical representative comparisons, rather than an additional choice of an abstract duality.

We pin down transposition on these models. For derived objects $U,V$, choose K-flat flat-term representatives $P_U,P_V$. Then $T(P_V)$ is K-injective and represents $H(V,\mathcal O)$. The tensor-descent theorem identifies $Q\operatorname{Tot}(P_U\otimes P_V)$ with $U\otimes^L V$. The K-injective Hom theorem and the global-Hom/homotopy theorem identify morphisms $U\to H(V,\mathcal O)$ and $U\otimes^L V\to\mathcal O$ with the respective homotopy classes of chain maps into $T(P_V)$ and $I$. The Hom-currying chain isomorphism identifies those classes. Its component is $c(g)(x\otimes y)=g(x)(y)$: for $|g|=n$, $|x|=p$, both differentials evaluate to $d_Ig(x)(y)-(-1)^ng(d_Px)(y)-(-1)^{n+p}g(x)(d_Py)$. Hence this is the specified tensor–Hom transposition, with no undetermined sign. Naturality of currying and tensor descent extend it through inverses of quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A96 (Hom from K-flat into K-injective); explicit currying differential.

proof.text:
Define $b_E:E\to T^2(E)$ by $b_E(x)(f)=(-1)^{pq}f(x)$ for $x\in E^p$ and $f\in T(E)^q$. This is a sheaf map since evaluation and the sign commute with restriction. Expanding the Hom differential gives
$$(d b_E(x))(f)=(-1)^{pq}d_I(f(x))-(-1)^{pq}(d_I(f(x))-(-1)^qf(d_Ex))=(-1)^{(p+1)q}f(d_Ex)=b_E(d_Ex)(f).$$
For a chain map $v:E\to E'$, evaluation of both $T^2(v)b_E(x)$ and $b_{E'}v(x)$ on $f$ gives $(-1)^{pq}f(v(x))$. Thus $b$ is a natural chain transformation, which descends by Step 1. Independently, the duality-map node gives the natural derived transformation $d$ defined as the transpose of coefficient evaluation with the Koszul symmetry. Steps 4–5 identify these two transformations on every object; the node's conditional ordinary-$\mathcal O[0]$ representative formula is not being applied to arbitrary complexes.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), explicit differential and naturality; Tag 08JD (lemma-dual), definition of the coefficient double-dual map.

proof.text: Let $P\to E$ be K-flat with flat terms, and resolve $T(P)$ by a K-flat flat-term complex $r:L\to T(P)$. The identity of $QT(P)$ is represented, using source $L$ and K-injective target $T(P)$, by $r$. The transposition of Step 2 therefore represents coefficient evaluation by $L\otimes P\to I$, $\ell\otimes x\mapsto r(\ell)(x)$. Tensor symmetry on total complexes is $x\otimes\ell\mapsto(-1)^{p q}\ell\otimes x$, where $|x|=p$, $|\ell|=q$. Substituting in the total differential verifies its chain-map property: the coefficients of $d\ell\otimes x$ and $\ell\otimes dx$ on both sides are respectively $(-1)^{pq}$ and $(-1)^{pq+q}$. Its square is the identity. The natural-transformation descent clause of the tensor-descent theorem gives this same symmetry on derived tensor.

source.place: Tags 08J9 and 0A97 (evaluation on K-flat/K-injective models), Section 06YL (derived tensor); explicit total-complex symmetry.

proof.text: The evaluation after symmetry in Step 4 is $x\otimes\ell\mapsto(-1)^{p q}r(\ell)(x)$. Its curry under Step 2 is $T(r)b_P$, since $(T(r)b_P(x))(\ell)=b_P(x)(r(\ell))=(-1)^{p q}r(\ell)(x)$. The comparison $T(r):T^2(P)\to T(L)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the well-definedness lemma. Consequently the transpose is exactly $Qb_P$ under the canonical representative comparison for $F(QP)$. For $P\to E$, naturality of $b$ (Step 3), naturality of $d$, and invertibility of this quasi-isomorphism give $Qb_E=d_{QE}$. This identifies the representative for arbitrary $E$ without assuming ordinary Hom into $\mathcal O[0]$ computes derived Hom.

source.place: Tags 0A95, 08J9, 08JD and 0A97; comparison of the explicit curry with the defining evaluation transpose.

proof.text:
Fix the signed comparisons by the explicit double-Hom cone lemma: $s_{E,m}:T(E[m])\to T(E)[-m]$ multiplies a degree-$q$ map by $(-1)^{mq}$, and
$$\chi_E=-s_{T(E),-1}\circ T(s_{E,1})^{-1}:T^2(E[1])\longrightarrow T^2(E)[1].$$
The leading minus sign is part of the normalization. The cited statement gives naturality in $E$, the component formula $(\chi_Eg)(y)=(-1)^{p+t}g(y)$ for $|g|=p$, $y\in T(E)^t$ (read on the right in degree $t+1$), and a natural cone isomorphism $\theta_u:T^2\operatorname{Cone}(u)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(T^2u)$. Its arrow identities are $\theta_u T^2(i)=i$ and $\chi_A T^2(-\pi)=-\pi\theta_u$. Together with the first arrow $T^2u$, they identify the $T^2$-image cone triangle with the cone triangle of $T^2u$. By Step 1 and the definition of distinguished triangles, $F$ is exact with the natural localized comparison $\psi=Q\chi$. Thus exactness is established for this precise comparison, independently of the unspecified existential comparison $e$ in the old shift lemma.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), omitted signs supplied by the cited explicit cone lemma.

proof.text:
For $x\in E[1]^p=E^{p+1}$ and $y\in T(E)^t$, regard $y$ in $T(E[1])^{t+1}$ without a sign. Then
$$(\chi_E b_{E[1]}(x))(y)=(-1)^{p+t+p(t+1)}y(x)=(-1)^{(p+1)t}y(x)=(b_E[1](x))(y).$$
Indeed the two exponents differ by $2p$. By Step 5 this gives $\psi_V d_{V[1]}=d_V[1]$. Iterating this equality defines coherent comparisons for positive integer shifts; taking the inverse shifted equality handles $[-1]$ and then all negative shifts. The comparison for shift zero is the identity. The identity and inverse constructions ensure coherence under addition of integers.

source.place: Tag 0A8X and explicit signed comparison in lem-sf-double-hom-cone-comparison; the displayed exponent calculation is the shift check.

proof.text:
For a distinguished triangle $V\xrightarrow{u}W\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}V[1]$, Step 6 makes its $F$-image distinguished with last arrow $\psi_V F(w)$. Apply the shift-compatible-natural-transformation triangle lemma to $\mathrm{id},F,d$, using naturality and Step 7. Explicitly the last square is
$$\psi_V F(w)d_Z=\psi_V d_{V[1]}w=d_V[1]w,$$
where the first equality is naturality at $w$. The other two squares are naturality at $u,v$. This supplies the asserted morphism of distinguished triangles with its connecting square.

source.place: Definitions 0144 and 014V (triangle morphism and image triangle), instantiated with the normalization established above.

proof.text:
Write $j^*$ for restriction to $\mathcal C/U$. Ordinary Hom complexes restrict by the componentwise identification
$$j^*\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^*E,j^*I).$$
To verify it, on an object $V\to U$ both sides in degree $n$ consist of families of module maps $E^a|_V\to I^{a+n}|_V$ on $\mathcal C/V$; relocalization identifies the two sites, and both differentials are $d_If-(-1)^nfd_E$. Restriction preserves products sectionwise. Also $j^*I$ is K-injective: for an acyclic complex $N$ on the slice, exactness of $j_!$ makes $j_!N$ acyclic; the termwise adjunction, applied to chain maps and their homotopies, identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(N,j^*I)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(j_!N,I)=0$. Exactness of $j^*$ makes $\mathcal O_U\to j^*I$ a resolution. Thus these componentwise Hom comparisons compute the canonical derived restriction comparison of the exactness/restriction node, using $j^*I$ on the slice. If the slice's fixed resolution is different, the canonical resolution comparisons in the derived-Hom definition identify the two models.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U), 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open); sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ; explicit sectionwise Hom comparison.

proof.text:
Let $\beta_V:j^*F(V)\cong F_U(j^*V)$ be the double-Hom comparison from Step 9. The formula for $s$ restricts to the same formula $f\mapsto(-1)^{mq}f$ on each $V'\to U$; reindexing and multiplication by $-1$ are unchanged. Restricting its inverse and applying $T$ is also componentwise precomposition. Hence, for the composite $\chi$ including its leading minus, one obtains the equality
$$\psi^U_{j^*V}\,\beta_{V[1]}=\beta_V[1],j^*\psi_V.$$
These formulas also respect a change of K-injective target $t:I\to J$: the two comparisons through $\mathcal Hom(T_I(E),J)$ send $b^I_E$ and $b^J_E$ to the same map, since $t((-1)^{pq}f(x))=(-1)^{pq}(t f)(x)$. The $s$ and $\chi$ formulas commute with both precomposition by $\mathcal Hom(E,t)$ and postcomposition by $t$, because their signs depend only on degrees. For a quasi-isomorphism $t$, both comparison arrows are quasi-isomorphisms by the well-definedness lemma. The same calculation applies to zigzags between fixed resolutions, so the displayed shift equality holds for the slice's specified model as well. The restriction clause of the duality-map node gives $\beta_V j^*d_V=d^U_{j^*V}$. For the connecting arrow, naturality of $\beta$ now gives
$$\psi^U F_U(j^*w)d^U_{j^*Z}=\psi^U\beta_{V[1]}j^*(F(w)d_Z)=\beta_V[1]j^*(\psi_VF(w)d_Z)=d^U_{j^*V}[1]j^*w.$$
Restriction is exact and commutes with the shift and cone formulas degreewise, so it takes distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. The same naturality equality for $u,v$ supplies the other two squares. This proves the precise slice connecting-square assertion.

source.place: Tags 08JB and 08JD, with the explicit s and chi formulas; derived.tex Tag 014E (restriction of cones).

proof.text: The closed tensor–Hom adjunction makes tensoring additive: tensorRight is a left adjoint and hence preserves finite coproducts, and symmetry transfers additivity to tensorLeft. The central unit-action formula for a scalar identity, together with associator and right-unitor coherence, makes tensorLeft linear; symmetry gives the same for tensorRight. Transpose the source-naturality equation for evaluation. Since both tensor variables are additive and linear, the contravariant internal-Hom functor preserves sums and scalar multiplication. Apply this twice to obtain additivity and linearity of the actual bidual, then use injectivity of underlying full-subcategory morphisms to obtain subcategory_linearity. This is a direct closed-category argument, so no localization-fraction calculation is needed in this step.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (componentwise O-linear Hom action), Section 08J7 (localization); explicit central-scalar calculation.

proof.text: Because the full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal T$ is preserved by duality, $F$ restricts to it. Extend this $R$-linear functor to its raw scalar localization by $\overline F(f\otimes a)=F(f)\otimes a$ and extend $d,\psi$ by $\overline d_V=d_V\otimes1$, $\overline\psi_V=\psi_V\otimes1$. These formulas respect tensor balancing by Step 11. Naturality on $f\otimes a$ is the original naturality equation tensored with $a$; additivity gives it on all morphisms. The shift square is its original equality tensored with $1$. By the scalar-localization triangulated lemma every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to the localization of an original one. The functor $\overline F$ takes that original image to the localization of its $F$-image, which is distinguished by Step 6. Functoriality and naturality extend this conclusion, and the triangle morphism from Step 8, across the specified triangle isomorphism. Thus $\overline F$ is exact with $\overline\psi$, and $\overline d$ has all three commuting squares on every localized distinguished triangle, including triangles whose arrows are fractions.

source.place: Scalar-localization construction and its specified distinguished triangles; blueprint lem-coef-rational-retract-evaluation, proof paragraph 3 (extension of the canonical comparisons).

proof.text: Apply triangle two-out-of-three to the exact functors $\mathrm{id},F$ and their shift-compatible natural transformation $d$, as established in Steps 6–8. It proves that any two invertible components among $d_V,d_W,d_Z$ force the third. Apply the same lemma to $\mathrm{id},\overline F,\overline d$ using Step 12 to obtain all three cases in $\mathcal T[1/s]$. The equation $\psi_Vd_{V[1]}=d_V[1]$ and invertibility of $\psi$ show that invertibility of $d_V$ is equivalent to that of $d_{V[1]}$; the inverse shift gives all integer shifts. The same equation holds after localization. None of these implications asserts that every component is invertible.
